title: Country Size Comparison: True Sizes, Same Scale
description: Use Country Size Comparison to see two countries side by side at one true scale — Russia is 24.6 times Texas, and Africa is 14 Greenlands. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, Africa covers about 30.4 million km² and Greenland 2.17 million — Africa is 14 times larger, however equal they look on a classroom Mercator wall map.
quick_answer: Country Size Comparison puts any two countries side by side at exactly the same map scale, with their true areas in square kilometres and a plain-language ratio. Pick two and see how big they really are — not how big the Mercator projection pretends they are.
steps_intro: Same scale, honest areas — here is how to read the comparison:

body.t: Most people met the world on a projection that inflates high latitudes. One comparison — Russia against a familiar US state — recalibrates intuition permanently. The
outlines show the same honest shapes for printing.
Ask the class which is bigger, Greenland or India, then run it: India wins by about 1.5 times, and the room gasps. That gasp is the lesson plan.
Moving from Germany to Texas? Texas alone is about twice Germany. Comparing your home country with a destination sets honest expectations about distances and driving days.
“Bigger than France” claims in headlines deserve a check. This tool is the two-click fact-check — and the
measures custom regions when countries are not the unit.
On a Mercator map Greenland rivals Africa. In truth Africa is about 14.0 times Greenland's area — and India (3.29 million km²) alone is about 1.5 times Greenland (2.17 million km²).
Texas is famously huge — and still only about 1.26 times metropolitan France (695,662 km² against 551,695 km²). Alaska, at 2.47 times Texas, is the comparison that ends arguments.

faq: Why does Russia look cut off in some views?

Russia spans about 180 degrees of longitude — any flat world view must cut somewhere, and the Pacific-centred cut splits Russia's far east. The comparison here draws each country whole, centred on itself, so nothing is amputated.
Which projection does the comparison use?

Each outline is drawn on its own local, equal-treatment basis at a shared ground scale — the point is that a kilometre is a kilometre in both panels. No single flat world projection can promise that, which is why the tool avoids one.

Follow the area figures' convention: totals are the commonly published ones for each country. France is the classic case — metropolitan France is 551,695 km², while the Republic including overseas lands is larger; the tool labels which figure it uses.
Can I compare a country with a US state?
Yes — states are in the list precisely because 'the size of Texas' is the world's favourite unit. Alaska at 1,717,854 km² is about 3.11 times metropolitan France.
Why do sources disagree on country areas?
Coastline measurement, inland water, tidal flats and disputed borders all move the last percent. For bar-room and classroom purposes the published totals agree far beyond the precision anyone needs.
What is the smallest comparison worth making?

Any you like — the ratio between Liechtenstein and Monaco is just as honest. Tiny states make the point that area rankings run from Russia's 17.1 million km² down to Vatican City's half a square kilometre.
Can I overlay one country on another instead?
Side-by-side is this tool's honest format: same scale, no distortion from forcing one shape inside another. For a drawn region's own area, use the Map Area Calculator.
